what: Telus is one of Canada's three big telecom carriers, selling mobile, internet and television subscriptions, and it also owns a large health services arm and a customer-support outsourcing business.
customers: Canadian households and businesses on subscription contracts, plus corporate clients of its health and digital services arms.
money: home internet, TV and business connectivity
benefits administration, virtual care and farm software
outsourced customer service and AI data work
moat: A fibre and wireless network that costs billions to build and that a new entrant cannot copy, in a market with three national carriers and a regulator that limits how many there can be.
risks: Price wars in Canadian mobile have been cutting the revenue earned per subscriber
Debt of about $20.7B against a market value of $17.2B, at a time when interest costs are high
The dividend has grown faster than free cash flow, which is how payout cuts start
opportunities: Free cash flow of $1.4B still covers the business even in a year with an accounting loss
The health arm sells into employer benefits and virtual care, a market growing much faster than telecom
Capital spending is falling now that the main fibre build is largely finished, which frees cash
watch: Revenue per mobile subscriber, and whether the dividend stays covered by free cash flow.
